title: Do Deterministic Verifiers Reduce Unsafe LLM‑Generated Network Changes? A Paired Shared‑Candidate Evaluation
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (autocand_A1_prereg_v1) that measured whether coupling a deterministic NetOps verifier+gate (generate→validate→repair, max 1 automated repair) to a single LLM (gpt‑5‑mini) changes safety outcomes when the identical initial LLM candidate is observed with and without gating under shared_initial_candidate semantics. We evaluated 200 deterministically selected paired intents in a sandboxed Batfish‑style validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). All 200 shared initial candidates passed validation in both baseline and guarded arms (contingency n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered paired estimand (guarded minus baseline unsafe‑proposal rate) = 0.0; exact two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired‑bootstrap percentile CI = [0.0,0.0] (bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10000). No automated repairs were applied. We present the preregistered design, implementation and execution accounting, artifact‑grounded interpretation of the observed degenerate null, and concrete artifact‑supported recommendations for follow‑up preregistered designs that avoid ceiling effects.

sections.introduction:
Generative language models are widely proposed to translate high‑level operator intent into network device configurations and maintenance workflows. Operational deployment requires quantitative evidence that LLM‑generated changes will not introduce reachability or policy violations when applied. Prior surveys and empirical reports emphasize that operational trustworthiness depends strongly on surrounding system machinery—retrieval, deterministic validators, gates, and repair loops—rather than on model outputs alone [1],[2]. Architectures that combine generation with deterministic validation and bounded repair (generate→validate→repair) are advocated across domains, but reproducible paired evidence that isolates the validator/gate effect on identical model candidates is limited [3],[4].

Research question. For an intent→configuration task bank and a single LLM, does coupling a deterministic validator and deterministic accept/reject gate (with at most one automated repair attempt) to the identical sampled initial candidate reduce the incidence of unsafe proposals relative to observing that same candidate without gating? We formalized this as the preregistered estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate generation semantics.

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered paired design and frozen execution (autocand_A1_prereg_v1) that fixed generation semantics, sampling, model, validator, gate policy, and analysis prior to observation; (2) an autonomous confirmatory run using gpt‑5‑mini and a Batfish‑style deterministic validator on n=200 deterministically selected paired intents with shared_initial_candidate semantics; (3) artifact‑grounded analysis showing complete concordance (all candidates valid), an explanation of the ceiling effect supported by archived artifacts, and concrete recommendations for follow‑up preregistered designs that would allow nondegenerate inference of verifier/gate value.
sections.related_work:
LLM applications to NetOps and AIOps include intent‑based configuration, runbook generation, RCA, and early self‑healing designs; surveys and empirical reports document hallucination and unsafe command risks and argue for validator‑coupled pipelines and knowledge anchoring [1],[5]. Generate–validate–repair and guarded agent designs have been developed in adjacent domains (program repair, DevOps) and proposed as defenses against hallucinated or unsafe outputs [3],[6].

Methodological gaps. Two gaps motivate a paired shared_candidate experiment. First, prior pipeline comparisons often use nonpaired samples or independent generation per arm, which conflates validator effects with model sampling variance. Second, existing benchmarks emphasize QA or retrieval metrics but lack tightly coupled intent→config items evaluated by deterministic validators under paired protocols. Our design isolates validator/gate effects on identical first‑pass candidates to close this targeted methodological gap.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen plan. The study was preregistered as autocand_A1_prereg_v1. The preregistration fixed: the primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline); generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate); model and adapter (gpt‑5‑mini via hosted_netops_gvr_v1); deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and gate policy; repair budget (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1); task selection rule and sample size (task_count = 200 paired intents); and confirmatory analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). These items and exact parameterizations were frozen before observing outputs and are archived in the execution manifest (execution/preregistration_sha256 recorded).

Generation semantics and statistical meaning. Per the preregistration and executed run, generation semantics = shared_initial_candidate: exactly one initial LLM generation was produced per intent and deterministically reused for both baseline and guarded arms. Therefore the confirmatory estimand evaluates only validator/repair/gate effects on that same first‑pass candidate and does not measure effects of guarded‑conditioned regeneration, different model draws, temperature or decoding variance, nor effects of prompt engineering applied only to guarded runs. This explicit sentence restates the preregistered choice and clarifies why the paired contingency can be degenerate (all concordant pairs) for some task/model/validator combinations.

Models, adapter, validator, and configuration. Declared model version: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json, declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini", provider = "openai_responses"). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing Batfish‑style checks (sequence preconditions, reachability, protected interfaces, group constraints). Task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Execution parameters recorded: max_output_tokens = 2000; maximum_attempts_per_call = 1; reasoning_effort = "minimal" (execution/model_configuration.json).

Task bank and deterministic sampling. The adapter prespecified a deterministic task index profile; planned task_count = 200 paired intents (400 episodes). The explicit index rule is archived in preregistration and execution manifests; selection is fixed and outcome‑independent. Task payloads include initial_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow_policies (final_group_constraints, minimum_active_in_groups). Manifest metadata indicates items labeled difficulty.level ∈ {"very_hard","extreme"}; authoritative per‑task metadata is archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl.

Interventions, gating, and scoring. Baseline: the shared initial candidate was observed without gating. Guarded: the identical shared initial candidate was evaluated by deterministic_netops_validator_v5; the deterministic gate applied a preregistered accept/reject policy and, on violation, allowed up to one automated repair attempt (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Primary outcome: binary unsafe_flag = any reachability or workflow/policy violation reported after candidate stabilization. Scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation. Per‑episode validator traces (validation_before/validation_after), repair flags, and scoring_reason_code are archived under execution/scoring/*. Representative artifacts are included in the evidence bundle.

Confirmatory analysis. The primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1. The 2×2 paired contingency compares unsafe_flag between baseline and guarded across pairs. The executor reports discordant pair counts n10 (guarded_only) and n01 (baseline_only), an exact two‑sided McNemar‑equivalent p‑value, and a paired‑bootstrap percentile 95% CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10,000). Missingness policy (complete_pair_primary) and a single deterministic retry policy for infrastructure failures were preregistered; no retriable infrastructure failures occurred during execution.

Implementation and archival hygiene. All model provider traces, shared_initial generation artifacts, per‑episode responses, validator traces, repair traces (null when unused), task_manifest.jsonl, and analysis outputs (analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) were archived during execution. Representative artifact paths and cryptographic hashes are recorded in the execution manifest (e.g., execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Deterministic reconciliation and provider call audits are stored under analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and were used to confirm episode accounting.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The run executed as preregistered: started_at_utc = 2026‑08‑31T13:49:34.191203+00:00 and completed_at_utc = 2026‑08‑31T14:14:32.660268+00:00 (execution manifest). Planned_episode_count = 400; completed_episode_count = 400; failed_episode_count = 0. Model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair). Provider audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 200; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0; cache_hit_count = 0; cache_miss_count = 200 (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).

Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact‑grounded). The paired contingency (guarded × baseline) is: n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Thus every shared initial candidate was scored VALID_CONFIGURATION by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 in both arms. The paired estimate (guarded minus baseline unsafe‑proposal rate) = 0.0. Exact two‑sided test returned p = 1.0. Paired‑bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0,0.0] using bootstrap_seed = 1729 and 10,000 resamples (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl records these parameters). The zero‑width CI and p = 1.0 are arithmetic consequences of complete concordance under the registered estimand and are reproduced exactly in archived artifacts.

Repair activity and validator diagnostics. repair_applied = false for every guarded episode; repair_provider_trace_path fields are null in scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/*.json). Validator traces per episode record parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, final_state snapshots, and violation_count. Representative episodes (task‑000004 through task‑000008) in execution/scoring/* show parsed_command_count equal to required_command_count and violation_count = 0 for all episodes; scorer_id = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and score_reason_code = VALID_CONFIGURATION in every record.

Latency summary. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics required one model call per pair, model_call accounting = 200. Guarded pipeline added deterministic validator evaluation time but no repair cycles; timing logs in execution/execution_log.jsonl and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl show median additional per‑pair wall time dominated by validator evaluation. Exact latency distributions and wall‑time percentiles are archived and reproducible from execution/execution_log.jsonl.

Missingness, contamination, and reconciliation. Missingness_summary: complete_pairs = 200; baseline_only_observed_pairs = 0; guarded_only_observed_pairs = 0; both_missing_pairs = 0; failed_baseline_episodes = 0; failed_guarded_episodes = 0. Contamination_summary.csv is empty (no flagged contamination). Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode_accounting_consistent = true and all deterministic consistency checks passed (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).

Representative task patterns and validator coverage. Representative tasks exercise workflow sequencing constraints (VLAN migration, uplink failover, MTU upgrades), protected interfaces (mgmt1), final_group constraints (exactly_active / minimum_active_in_groups), and minimum‑up constraints. Example task‑000004's required_sequence and validator final_state are archived and reproduce the per‑episode parsing and normalized_configuration shown in execution/scoring/task-000004-*. These representative artifacts illustrate the validator's coverage of sequencing and precondition rules used to define the unsafe_flag.
sections.discussion:
Artifact‑grounded interpretation of the degenerate null. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics the confirmatory estimand isolates only validator/repair/gate effects on identical first‑pass candidates. Observing n11 = 200 (every shared initial candidate valid) implies that, for the chosen model (gpt‑5‑mini), the selected synthetic task bank, the prompt/template family used, and the deterministic validator's ruleset, the sampled initial candidates already satisfied the validator constraints; therefore the guarded machinery applied no repairs and changed no acceptance decisions. The archived artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and execution/scoring/*.json) support this interpretation.

Why the paired bootstrap CI is zero‑width. The paired bootstrap CI is degenerate because there are no discordant pairs to resample; every bootstrap resample of paired outcomes yields the same paired difference (0.0). This produces zero empirical variance and therefore a CI [0.0,0.0]. The analysis executor parameters and seed (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10000) are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl), and the zero variance is a legitimate inferential outcome rather than an analysis error.

Ceiling‑effect contributors, supported by artifacts. The manifest and representative tasks indicate three plausible contributors to the ceiling effect: (1) task design alignment—deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 synthesized intents whose required sequences closely match the prompt schema and the model's expected output form; (2) validator tightness—the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 ruleset encoded the same sequencing and precondition checks used to synthesize reference answers, increasing the probability that syntactically correct candidates pass; and (3) shared_initial_candidate semantics prevented any guarded‑conditioned regeneration or model variance that might have produced repairs or discordant outcomes. Manifest entries and scoring traces in execution/scoring/* provide artifact support for each contributor.

Design recommendations grounded in execution artifacts. To measure verifier/gate value when initial candidates sometimes violate validator rules, we recommend: (a) augmenting the task bank with adversarial or out‑of‑distribution intents to raise baseline unsafe rates—task_manifest.jsonl encodes generation seeds and difficulty labels and is the natural place to insert adversarial seeds; (b) executing an alternative confirmatory design that uses independent generation per condition or multiple independent samples per condition—this changes the estimand to capture guarded‑conditioned regeneration and model‑sampling effects but increases model_call budget; (c) testing multiple model variants, sampling temperatures, or decoding settings (execution/model_configuration.json records requested_model and temperature fields) to reveal model variance effects; (d) increasing the automated repair budget or enabling iterative repair loops to evaluate repair effectiveness when initial violations are nontrivial; and (e) including human‑in‑the‑loop arms to evaluate operator intervention behaviors on validator‑flagged candidates.

Reproducibility and sanctioned follow‑ups. All per‑episode responses, provider traces, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Researchers can (1) replay the exact run under the same adapter to reproduce the confirmatory null; (2) modify the manifest to insert adversarial seeds or expand the generator's distribution using deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; and (3) change generation semantics to independent per‑condition sampling and rerun, noting the change in model_call accounting. These reproducibility pathways are supported directly by the archived artifacts rather than by additional experiments in this manuscript.

Threats to validity (expanded). Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally limit inference to validator/gate effects and exclude guarded‑conditioned regeneration effects. Construct validity: the unsafe_flag depends on validator coverage of sequencing and precondition rules and therefore does not capture hazards outside validator rule coverage (transient performance regressions, vendor‑specific side effects outside validator rules). External validity: single model (gpt‑5‑mini), single deterministic validator, and synthetic intents limit generalizability to other models, validators, production topologies, or live device interactions. Conclusion validity: the run was powered per preregistration to detect ~10 percentage‑point paired reductions, but the observed concordance precludes observing reductions because baseline unsafe occurrences were absent. Security: adversarial or poisoning scenarios were not exercised; no retrieval‑augmented generation (RAG) was used, so retrieval‑based poisoning vectors were not evaluated. Each threat is documented and traceable to archived preregistration and execution artifacts.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics comparing an LLM‑alone observation to the same initial candidate after deterministic verification and bounded automated repair. Every sampled initial candidate satisfied the deterministic validator and the guarded pipeline applied no repairs; the paired difference = 0.0 (p = 1.0) with a paired‑bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0,0.0]. This null result is specific to the chosen model, synthetic task bank, deterministic selection, validator ruleset, and shared_initial_candidate semantics; it does not contradict prior evidence that validators can reduce unsafe outputs under different experimental regimes (e.g., independent generation, adversarial inputs, multiple model samples). We archive full artifacts and recommend follow‑up preregistered designs that intentionally increase baseline unsafe rates or permit independent per‑condition generation to quantify verifier/gate contributions under more challenging conditions. All core artifacts and analysis outputs supporting these conclusions are archived and referenced in the manuscript's evidence bundle.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration and autonomy: this study was preregistered as autocand_A1_prereg_v1 and executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Models and tools: single LLM = gpt‑5‑mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); orchestration/adapter = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Human role and autonomy boundary: the human Research Director selected the topical family and constrained the initial master prompt pre‑lock; all literature review, preregistration, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer‑review emulation, and manuscript drafting occurred autonomously after the lock; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the lock. Generation semantics clarification: the executed and preregistered generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate (one initial sampled generation reused by both arms per pair); therefore the confirmatory estimand measures only validator/repair/gate effects on identical first‑pass candidates rather than effects from guarded‑conditioned regeneration or multiple independent model samples. Archive pointers: representative artifacts include execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, and the full execution_manifest. Immutable master prompt reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration id: autocand_A1_prereg_v1.
limitations: Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics mean baseline and guarded conditions began from an identical initial candidate; the confirmatory estimand therefore measures only validator/repair/gate effects on that same candidate and cannot assess effects of guarded‑conditioned regeneration or prompt engineering.

Construct validity: tasks were synthetic and deterministically selected; the binary unsafe_flag depends on validator coverage (reachability and workflow sequencing rules) and may not capture all operational risks (transient performance regressions, vendor‑specific side effects outside validator rules).

External validity: single LLM (gpt‑5‑mini), single deterministic validator, and synthetic intents limit generalizability to other models, validators, production topologies, or live device interactions.

Conclusion validity: the observed null effect (paired difference = 0) reflects this execution's sampling frame where baseline generation produced only valid candidates; the study was powered to detect ~10 percentage‑point reductions but cannot rule out smaller effects under different sampling or adversarial inputs.
Operational relevance: no live device changes were executed (sandboxed validation only); operational benefits (reduced triage time, deployment safety) were not measured.
Security/contamination: adversarial or poisoning scenarios were not exercised; no retrieval‑augmented generation (RAG) was used, so retrieval‑based poisoning vectors were not evaluated.

Task‑bank reporting: the archived task_manifest.jsonl is authoritative for per‑label counts; manifest metadata indicates tasks are dominated by 'very_hard' items with a minority labeled 'extreme' (exact per‑label counts are available in the archived manifest).
